Q1: /afk:setup loads the whole register, classifies each row, and builds the election from the register at run time, never from a hardcoded list; [opt-in] rows join it deselected by default on every branch.

Q1: set_instruction_files.py merges only pluginConfigs.agents-md@builtin.options.instructionFiles into $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json or ~/.claude/settings.json, writes a backup and then a plain write, and writes no permission rule; H11 runs it as probe (--check) and auto fix.
Q1: row H7 renders BEHAVIORS.md with behavior_registry.py render and installs the afk:behaviors block with install_block.py into each verified provider target; teardown removes it.

Q2: plugin-source-gates.sh runs skill-registry, native-contract, genericity and behavior-registry; precommit-gates.sh runs it on the staged tree for agent commits in the plugin repository only, and pull-request CI runs it twice by range (target tip, then the branch).

Q2: native check A reads skills/afk/setup/MANIFEST.md and CHANGELOG.md (only PROVIDERS.md, CAPABILITIES.md, two providers/ files and docs/afk/ are skipped) and refuses a harness name unless a native-contract-allow.txt line matches.
Q2: native check C compares skill directories with both plugin.json manifests and never reads the register; native check K lets only providers/<name>.sh name a <name>_*.py helper.

Q2: the register reader for env vars is skill-registry check C, and it reads only hooks/*.sh and hooks/lib/*.sh, so a constant (plain or self-default) in hooks/lib/providers/claude.sh is never judged; the design's claim that a self-default fails check C (SDD.md:1487, plan 0009:28) is refuted.

claims.text: Q1: no code reads or writes a permission allow rule or AFK_SPAWN_ALLOW_RULE today; the only hits are in plan 0009.
Q1: hooks/lib/providers/claude.sh holds functions only, and provider.sh sources every providers/*.sh, so a new top-level constant is defined in every hook process of both harnesses.

Q3: the change breaks nothing that already exists; the same commit must add the constant to claude.sh, the register row, and one native-contract-allow.txt line for MANIFEST.md (and a CHANGELOG line pattern if the entry names the harness), else native check A blocks the agent commit and both CI runs.

Q3: tests that lift register rows by heading (test_setup_h6_probe.py, test_setup_secrets_repo_root.py, test_lavish_wave_host.py, hook-smoke.sh:208) stay green when the row has its own ### heading and avoids `no .afk/config.yaml` and `no config layer`.
Q3: the wait for the human and the no-human skip are agent prose with precedents (H6 needs-human, H12 never writes); no script or test enforces them, so they are unguarded.
Whether the harness honours the printed allow rule as written can only be shown by a live run (B14 frontier).

Setup builds the election at run time from MANIFEST.md: step 1 loads every entry, step 3 adds every [opt-in] row deselected by default on every branch, so one new opt-in row is probed and offered with no SKILL.md edit.

set_instruction_files.py merges one key, pluginConfigs.agents-md@builtin.options.instructionFiles, into the settings file CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude names, with a .bak and a plain non-atomic write; its readers are MANIFEST H11, hooks/agents-md-config-check.sh and their tests, and C19 touches none of them.

Row H7 renders the afk:behaviors block through behavior_registry.py render and install_block.py install, which writes the instruction file by atomic replace; hook-smoke.sh:208 pins the H7 heading and fence.

All four plugin-source gates read the candidate tree: agent commits run the installed copy's runner --staged (precommit-gates.sh:151-153), CI runs the target tip's runner then the branch's own --range (tests.yml:85, :99); so an allow line staged in the same commit is honoured by every judge.

Native check A reaches MANIFEST.md through a *.md glob, never by name: a row that writes 'Claude Code' fails unless hooks/native-contract-allow.txt gains a matching line; a row that writes 'H-1 harness' needs none.
Check K fails only when a file outside hooks/lib/providers/claude.sh names a claude_*.py helper; a row that sources claude.sh to print the constant passes K.

The design's clause 'a self-default in claude.sh fails check C until an E-table row lands' is wrong: the check that reads the E table is skill-registry check C, and its universe is hooks/*.sh and hooks/lib/*.sh only, so hooks/lib/providers/claude.sh is never read; native check C compares skills with the two plugin.json files.

Check C would still fail if any hooks/*.sh or hooks/lib/*.sh file read the constant as $NAME, plain assignment or not, because the assignment in hooks/lib/providers/claude.sh is outside the set check C builds; the design's planned readers (the MANIFEST row and scripts/team/permission.py) are outside that universe.
The genericity gate reaches MANIFEST.md through its changed-*.md scope and refuses the decision ids AUTO-1, AUTO-2 and INV-057 in an added row; S-246, T7b and H-1 pass.
hooks/lib/provider.sh sources every hooks/lib/providers/*.sh by glob, so the new constant in claude.sh is evaluated in every hook process that loads provider.sh; the seed's B3 sites omit this loader.
The new row must not reuse id H8 or H10: install_block.py, AUDIT.md, MANIFEST.md H7 and ADR-0005 use those ids for retired legacy blocks.
Whether 'skipped with no human present' holds in a hands-off run depends on the agent honouring deselected-by-default; SKILL.md names no non-interactive branch and no test pins the election.

With the edits plan/0009 lists (one hooks/native-contract-allow.txt line for a row naming the harness, a plain assignment in hooks/lib/providers/claude.sh, no claude_*.py name in the row, no ticket-shaped id), native checks A and K, skill-registry check C and the genericity gate pass with the new row, and every open gate and loader site needs no edit; without the allow line a row naming the harness fails check A and test_native_contract_events.py:57 goes red.
